what: copd: recovering a known programme effect
title: Health-economics datasets for teaching panel models
text: Question. Clinics 1 2 adopted care-management programme visit 3, clinics 3 4 visit 4, clinics 5 6 never . construction, programme cuts cost users 1 - exp(-0.5), 39 percent, sample average effect treated visits -406 euros (see ?copd). estimators find ? Interpretation. 60 patients Callaway Sant’Anna estimate imprecise (-184 euros, standard error 200): confidence interval covers true -406 euros, pre-trend test reject parallel trends, single small panel pin effect . two-part model far precise conditions exacerbations admissions, explain cost variation: programme coefficient log positive cost -0.52 (standard error 0.13) true value -0.5. Rerunning design large simulated panel (data-raw/copd.R ) brings estimators close truth; point known-truth teaching dataset.
code: idx <- c("id", "visit") att <- attgt(cost ~ 1, data = copd, index = idx, treat = "adopt",              control = "notyet") summary(att) #>  #> Callaway and Sant'Anna group-time ATT #> Aggregation: overall (simple weighted average) #> Control group: not yet treated  Estimator: unconditional  Individuals: 60  #>  #> ATT: -184 (SE 199.1, 95% CI -574.2 to 206.2) #>  #> Pre-trend test (pre-treatment ATT(g, t) = 0): Chi-squared = 2.116, df = 3, p-value = 0.5487  tp <- twopart(cost ~ exacerbations + hospitalized + smoker + treatment + crp +                 visit + programme + factor(clinic),               binary_formula = ~ exacerbations + hospitalized + smoker +                 treatment + crp,               data = copd, index = idx, positive = "lognormal") coef(tp$positive)[["programme"]] #> [1] -0.5178754

what: docvisits: state dependence in doctor use
title: Health-economics datasets for teaching panel models
text: Question. People saw doctor last year likely see one year. habit (true state dependence) persistent ill health (unobserved heterogeneity)? use consecutive waves 1984 1988 Wooldridge initial-conditions approach (dynamic = TRUE). Interpretation. pooled dynamic probit gives lagged-visit coefficient 0.65, mixes true state dependence persistent unobserved health. random-effects probit initial conditions shrinks 0.28 (roughly 8 percentage points probability scale, see partialeffects()), initial-condition coefficient random-effect variance absorb rest: apparent persistence heterogeneity, habit.
code: early <- subset(docvisits, year <= 1988) f <- doctor ~ age + hhninc + hhkids + married + working pooled <- panglm(f, data = early, index = c("id", "year"), model = "pooling",                  family = "probit", dynamic = TRUE, vcov = "cluster") random <- panglm(f, data = early, index = c("id", "year"), model = "random",                  family = "probit", dynamic = TRUE, R = 8) cbind(pooled = coef(pooled)[c("lag_doctor", "initial_doctor")],       random = coef(random)[c("lag_doctor", "initial_doctor")]) #>                   pooled    random #> lag_doctor     0.6453130 0.2824974 #> initial_doctor 0.5457217 0.9103464

what: meps: the spending gap of the uninsured
title: Health-economics datasets for teaching panel models
text: Question. much less uninsured adults spend health care, much cross-sectional gap survives compare person change coverage? Among people positive spending, pooled gamma model says uninsured spend 68 percent less; within estimate, identified people gained lost coverage 2018 2019, shrinks 31 percent less. Much cross-sectional gap reflects uninsured rather effect losing coverage.
code: tp <- twopart(totexp ~ insurance + I(age / 10) + sex + nchronic + povcat,               data = meps, index = c("id", "year"), positive = "gamma") partialeffects(tp, variables = "insurance") #>  #> Average partial effects (total mean) #> Delta-method standard errors, vcov: classical  #>  #>       term            contrast estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low #>  insurance    public - private   -503.2     728.1    -0.691 4.896e-01    -1930 #>  insurance uninsured - private  -6194.0     563.4   -10.990 4.086e-28    -7299 #>  conf.high #>        924 #>      -5090  pos <- subset(meps, totexp > 0) pooled <- panglm(totexp ~ insurance + povcat + I(age / 10) + sex + nchronic,                  data = pos, index = c("id", "year"), family = "gamma",                  model = "pooling") within <- panglm(totexp ~ insurance + povcat, data = pos,                  index = c("id", "year"), family = "gamma", model = "within") exp(c(pooled = coef(pooled)[["insuranceuninsured"]],       within = coef(within)[["insuranceuninsured"]])) - 1 #>     pooled     within  #> -0.6795660 -0.3096233

what: medicaid: staggered adoption of the Medicaid expansion
title: Health-economics datasets for teaching panel models
text: Question. Affordable Care Act Medicaid expansion reduce uninsurance among adults poverty line? Adoption staggered (2014 2019 within panel; later adopters ten non-adopters serve controls), single-coefficient two-way fixed effects regression may compare late adopters already-treated early adopters. attgt() builds clean comparisons never-treated states. Interpretation. Leads expansion small scattered around zero, supports parallel trends. uninsured share adults poverty line falls 5 percentage points year expansion 6 8 points two three years; overall group-time ATT -6.5 points (SE 1.3). Medicaid coverage adults rises 10 points, uninsurance falls: part gain replaces coverage (crowd-). two-way fixed effects estimate (-7.2) stays close robust ones (extended TWFE -7.1), treated states adopted 2014 effect fairly flat two years; spread-adoption stronger dynamics gap can large.
code: ix <- c("state", "year") cs <- attgt(uninspov ~ 1, data = medicaid, index = ix, treat = "adopt",             control = "never") summary(cs, type = "dynamic") #>  #> Callaway and Sant'Anna group-time ATT #> Aggregation: event study (by time since treatment) #> Control group: never treated  Estimator: unconditional  Individuals: 51  #>  #> ATT (mean of e >= 0): -6.562 (SE 1.317, 95% CI -9.143 to -3.98) #>  #>  event estimate     se     lower   upper #>     -9  0.97529 0.8140  -0.62013  2.5707 #>     -8 -0.09853 0.6997  -1.46999  1.2729 #>     -7  1.16922 1.0103  -0.81093  3.1494 #>     -6 -1.12859 1.1047  -3.29372  1.0365 #>     -5  1.48015 0.7483   0.01347  2.9468 #>     -4 -0.63116 0.4610  -1.53479  0.2725 #>     -3 -0.29785 0.5167  -1.31050  0.7148 #>     -2  0.40279 0.3635  -0.30965  1.1152 #>     -1 -0.38889 0.5469  -1.46071  0.6829 #>      0 -5.15564 0.9010  -6.92165 -3.3896 #>      1 -6.39822 1.2670  -8.88146 -3.9150 #>      2 -7.08836 1.3521  -9.73834 -4.4384 #>      3 -7.59013 1.4220 -10.37726 -4.8030 #>      4 -6.52274 1.5487  -9.55810 -3.4874 #>      5 -6.61563 1.8257 -10.19386 -3.0374  tw <- did(uninspov ~ 1, data = medicaid, index = ix, treat = "adopt") ew <- etwfe(uninspov ~ 1, data = medicaid, index = ix, treat = "adopt") c(attgt = summary(cs)$overall$estimate, etwfe = summary(ew)$overall$estimate,   twfe = coef(tw)[["treated"]]) #>     attgt     etwfe      twfe  #> -6.539795 -7.116279 -7.206276  # first stage: Medicaid coverage of the same adults summary(attgt(medicaidpov ~ 1, data = medicaid, index = ix,               treat = "adopt", control = "never"))$overall #>   estimate      se    lower   upper #> 1  10.2355 1.40579 7.480201 12.9908

what: healthspend: is health care a luxury?
title: Health-economics datasets for teaching panel models
text: Question. health spending rise proportionally national income (income elasticity 1)? Interpretation. Within countries, real health spending grows 1.15 percent 1 percent income, looks like luxury good, Mundlak test reject random effects. Adding year effects brings elasticity 0.84: much apparent luxury effect common upward trend spending across countries.
code: hs <- transform(healthspend, lche = log(chereal), lgdp = log(gdppc)) ix <- c("iso3c", "year") fe <- panglm(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, model = "within") re <- panglm(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, model = "random") fe2 <- panglm(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, model = "within",               effect = "twoways", vcov = "cluster") cbind(within = coef(fe), random = coef(re)[-1], twoways = coef(fe2)) #>       within   random   twoways #> lgdp 1.14926 1.135463 0.8396004 panhausman(fe, method = "mundlak", data = hs) #>  #>  Mundlak specification test (fixed vs. random effects), vcov: cluster #>  #> F = 1.463, df = 1, 185, p-value = 0.228 #> alternative hypothesis: one model is inconsistent

what: cigar: habits and the long-run price elasticity
title: Health-economics datasets for teaching panel models
text: Question. Cigarette demand addictive: strong habit, long-run price elasticity? lagged dependent variable makes pooled OLS biased upwards within estimator biased downwards (Nickell bias); difference GMM lie . Interpretation. habit coefficient difference GMM (0.84) lies within (0.83) OLS (0.97) estimates, theory predicts, three rows reproduce Table 8.1 Baltagi’s Econometric Analysis Panel Data. short-run price elasticity -0.38 long-run one -2.4.
code: ix <- c("state", "year") f <- lnc ~ lag(lnc, 1) + lnp + lnpn + lny ols <- panglm(f, data = cigar, index = ix, model = "pooling") fe <- panglm(f, data = cigar, index = ix, model = "within", effect = "twoways") ab <- pangmm(lnc ~ lag(lnc, 1) + lnp + lnpn + lny | lag(lnc, 2:99),              data = cigar, index = ix, transformation = "d", model = "onestep") #> Warning: 437 instruments for 46 individuals: too many instruments bias GMM #> toward OLS and weaken the Hansen test; use collapse = TRUE or a smaller maxlag tab <- rbind(OLS = coef(ols)[-1], Within = coef(fe), GMM = coef(ab)[1:4]) round(tab, 3) #>        lag(lnc, 1)    lnp   lnpn    lny #> OLS          0.969 -0.090  0.024 -0.031 #> Within       0.833 -0.299  0.034  0.100 #> GMM          0.843 -0.377 -0.016  0.139 round(tab[, "lnp"] / (1 - tab[, 1]), 2)  # long-run price elasticity #>    OLS Within    GMM  #>  -2.96  -1.79  -2.40

text: Patients buy private insurance health shock (need) also raises doctor visits, insurance correlated time-varying error within estimator biased. employer offer insurance shifts coverage direct effect visits, valid instrument. true effect insurance 0.6. formula y ~ regressors | instruments follows plm: exogenous regressors appear sides, regressor absent instrument list endogenous. within estimator gives 1.74, nearly three times true effect. Fixed-effects 2SLS gives 0.90 standard error 0.35, confidence interval covers 0.6. first-stage F statistic (68, also cluster-robust form) far usual threshold 10, instrument strong. IV estimates much less precise biased ones: price consistency. model = "random" gives random-effects 2SLS estimator (G2SLS Balestra Varadharajan-Krishnakumar 1987, EC2SLS Baltagi 1981 inst.method = "baltagi").
code: set.seed(1) N <- 300; TT <- 4 d <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(N), each = TT), wave = rep(seq_len(TT), N)) alpha <- rep(rnorm(N), each = TT)      # unobserved frailty s0 <- rep(rnorm(N), each = TT)         # family background need <- rnorm(N * TT)                  # time-varying health shock d$school <- round(12 + 2 * s0 + alpha) d$female <- rep(rbinom(N, 1, 0.5), each = TT) d$offer <- rbinom(N * TT, 1, plogis(s0)) d$income <- rnorm(N * TT) + 0.5 * alpha d$insured <- as.numeric(d$offer + need + rnorm(N * TT) > 0.5) d$visits <- 1 + 0.6 * d$insured + 0.2 * d$income + alpha + need +   rnorm(N * TT) coef(panglm(visits ~ insured + income, data = d, index = c("id", "wave"),             model = "within")) #>   insured    income  #> 1.7440674 0.2072374 fe2sls <- paniv(visits ~ insured + income | offer + income, data = d,                 index = c("id", "wave"), model = "within", vcov = "cluster") summary(fe2sls) #>  #> Call: #> paniv(formula = visits ~ insured + income | offer + income, data = d,  #>     index = c("id", "wave"), model = "within", vcov = "cluster") #>  #> Estimator: fixed-effects 2SLS  #> n = 1200  groups = 300  vcov: cluster  #> Endogenous: insured  #> Excluded instruments: offer  #>  #> Coefficients: #>         Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> insured   0.9011     0.3470   2.597  0.00942 **  #> income    0.2100     0.0440   4.773 1.82e-06 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> First stage (excluded instruments): #>         partial.R2     F df1 df2   p.value F.robust  p.robust #> insured    0.06976 67.34   1 898 7.882e-16    68.02 5.188e-15 #> Residual df: 898

what: Dynamic panels: difference and system GMM
title: Endogeneity: IV, Hausman-Taylor, GMM and selection
text: last period’s outcome enters model, habit persistence smoking, lagged outcome correlated individual effect (pooled OLS overstates persistence) , within transformation, demeaned error (fixed effects understates , Nickell 1981). GMM estimators use deeper lags outcome instruments: difference GMM (Arellano Bond 1991) model first differences, system GMM (Blundell Bond 1998) adds model levels lagged differences instruments. true persistence 0.5 price effect -0.3. formula follows plm::pgmm(): regressors, GMM-style instruments. lag(cigs, 2:99) uses available lags second . estimates close 0.5. diagnostics read Arellano-Bond tests, AR(1) differenced residuals expected AR(2) must rejected (p = 0.34), Hansen test overidentifying restrictions. two-step standard errors use Windmeijer (2005) correction. Finite-sample bias. GMM consistent number individuals grows, moderate samples can badly biased, matching another package protect . many instruments overfit endogenous regressor pull estimate toward pooled OLS, making Hansen test look good (Roodman 2009). variance individual effect large, level moments system GMM become weak (Bun Windmeijer 2010). Practical rules: prefer two-step estimator; use collapse = TRUE small maxlag, instrument count stays well number individuals (pangmm() warns ; uncollapsed fit already uses 21 instruments 7 waves); treat Hansen p-value close 1 (0.96 ) warning sign, support; check persistence estimate lies fixed-effects (biased ) pooled OLS (biased ) estimates (Bond 2002). panglm() create panel lags formula, build lagged outcome first bounds. GMM estimates fall inside bounds.
code: set.seed(1) N <- 300; TT <- 7 g <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(N), each = TT), wave = rep(seq_len(TT), N)) propensity <- rnorm(N) g$price <- rnorm(N * TT) g$cigs <- NA for (i in seq_len(N)) {   r <- (i - 1) * TT + seq_len(TT)   y <- propensity[i] / 0.5 + rnorm(1)   for (t in seq_len(TT)) {     y <- 0.5 * y - 0.3 * g$price[r[t]] + propensity[i] + rnorm(1)     g$cigs[r[t]] <- y   } } ab <- pangmm(cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99), data = g,              index = c("id", "wave"), model = "twostep") summary(ab) #>  #> Call: #> pangmm(formula = cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99),  #>     data = g, index = c("id", "wave"), model = "twostep") #>  #> Estimator: two-way two-step difference GMM (Arellano-Bond)  #> n = 1500  groups = 300  T = 7  instruments = 21  #> vcov: robust (Windmeijer)  #>  #> Coefficients: #>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> lag(cigs, 1)  0.55025    0.04883  11.268   <2e-16 *** #> price        -0.27276    0.03055  -8.927   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Arellano-Bond AR(1) test: z = -10.24, p = < 2.2e-16 #> Arellano-Bond AR(2) test: z = -0.9451, p = 0.3446 #> Sargan test (not robust): chi2(14) = 7.391, p = 0.9186 #> Hansen J test (robust): chi2(14) = 6.259, p = 0.9595 #> Wald test for coefficients: chi2(2) = 194.5, p = < 2.2e-16 bb <- pangmm(cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99), data = g,              index = c("id", "wave"), transformation = "ld",              model = "twostep", collapse = TRUE, maxlag = 4) summary(bb) #>  #> Call: #> pangmm(formula = cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99),  #>     data = g, index = c("id", "wave"), transformation = "ld",  #>     model = "twostep", collapse = TRUE, maxlag = 4) #>  #> Estimator: two-way two-step system GMM (Blundell-Bond)  #> n = 3300  groups = 300  T = 7  instruments = 12  #> vcov: robust (Windmeijer)  #>  #> Coefficients: #>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> lag(cigs, 1)  0.50920    0.03825  13.313   <2e-16 *** #> price        -0.26263    0.02786  -9.428   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Arellano-Bond AR(1) test: z = -8.576, p = < 2.2e-16 #> Arellano-Bond AR(2) test: z = -1.041, p = 0.2978 #> Sargan test (not robust): chi2(4) = 5.905, p = 0.2064 #> Hansen J test (robust): chi2(4) = 4.635, p = 0.3269 #> Wald test for coefficients: chi2(2) = 268.8, p = < 2.2e-16 g$cigs_lag <- ave(g$cigs, g$id, FUN = function(v) c(NA, head(v, -1))) gl <- g[!is.na(g$cigs_lag), ] ols <- panglm(cigs ~ cigs_lag + price, data = gl, index = c("id", "wave"),               model = "pooling") fe <- panglm(cigs ~ cigs_lag + price, data = gl, index = c("id", "wave"),              model = "within") c(fixed_effects = coef(fe)[["cigs_lag"]],   difference_gmm = coef(ab)[["lag(cigs, 1)"]],   system_gmm = coef(bb)[["lag(cigs, 1)"]],   pooled_ols = coef(ols)[["cigs_lag"]]) #>  fixed_effects difference_gmm     system_gmm     pooled_ols  #>      0.2311729      0.5502465      0.5091996      0.8431146

Fixed effects respondents gives 0.35 true 0.5. corrected estimate 0.45, joint test inverse Mills ratio coefficients zero rejects clearly, selection time-varying shock matters . test uses cluster-robust covariance, valid null hypothesis; coefficient standard errors use bootstrap, accounts first step.

title: Policy evaluation: DiD, event studies and staggered adoption
text: Half 200 practices adopt care pathway 2019. Visits follow common upward trend, pathway adds 1 visit adoption 0.3 year . () adds indicator treated, 1(t >= first), model unit year fixed effects. single adoption date coefficient average treatment effect treated (ATT) parallel trends. pathway adds 1.7 visits per year average four post-adoption years (true value 1.45). binary outcome, family = "binomial" fits conditional (fixed-effects) logit year effects, coefficient log odds ratio; "poisson" "negbin" available counts. odds admission double adoption (true odds ratio e0.8=2.2e^{0.8} = 2.2). Practices never always admitted carry information conditional likelihood dropped. eventstudy() replaces single indicator one indicator per year relative adoption, year adoption reference. leads (negative event times) test parallel pre-trends; lags trace effect time.  leads close zero jointly significant (p = 0.74); effect rises 1.1 adoption 1.9 three years later. non-significant pre-trend test proof parallel trends: limited power (Roth 2022).
code: set.seed(1) d <- expand.grid(id = 1:200, year = 2015:2022) d$first <- ifelse(d$id <= 100, 2019, NA) a <- rnorm(200) e <- d$year - d$first post <- !is.na(e) & e >= 0 d$visits <- 3 + a[d$id] + 0.1 * (d$year - 2015) +   ifelse(post, 1 + 0.3 * e, 0) + rnorm(nrow(d)) d$admitted <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, plogis(-1 + a[d$id] +                                           0.05 * (d$year - 2015) + 0.8 * post)) fit <- did(visits ~ 1, data = d, index = c("id", "year"), treat = "first") coef(fit) #>  treated  #> 1.664368 confint(fit) #>         2.5 %   97.5 % #> treated 1.471 1.857735 fitb <- did(admitted ~ 1, data = d, index = c("id", "year"),             treat = "first", family = "binomial") #> 16 group(s) with no within-group outcome variation dropped (all-0 or all-1) -- they carry no information for the conditional likelihood. exp(cbind(OR = coef(fitb), confint(fitb))) #>               OR    2.5 %   97.5 % #> treated 2.020067 1.300451 3.137888 es <- eventstudy(visits ~ 1, data = d, index = c("id", "year"),                  treat = "first", leads = 4, lags = 3) es #>  #> Event study (two-way fixed effects, gaussian) #> n = 1600  groups = 200  vcov: cluster  #> Reference event time: -1 (end points binned)  #>  #>  event   estimate     se   lower  upper #>     -4 -0.0279406 0.2023 -0.4245 0.3686 #>     -3 -0.0006271 0.2125 -0.4170 0.4158 #>     -2 -0.2058470 0.2117 -0.6209 0.2092 #>     -1  0.0000000 0.0000  0.0000 0.0000 #>      0  1.1355992 0.2152  0.7139 1.5573 #>      1  1.7096956 0.2064  1.3051 2.1143 #>      2  1.6908680 0.1949  1.3089 2.0728 #>      3  1.8868941 0.2176  1.4604 2.3134 #>  #> Pre-trend test: Chi-squared = 1.248, df = 3, p-value = 0.7414 plot(es)

text: Gaussian within fits: alpha_i = ybar_i - xbar_i' beta, intercepts least-squares dummy-variable regression. normalized: fixest::fixef() gives values model without intercept. Poisson within fits: conditional (Poisson fixed-effects) estimator estimate alpha_i, individual intercept maximizes unconditional likelihood conditional beta closed form alpha_i = log(sum_t y_it / sum_t exp(x_it' beta)), values reported fixest::fepois(). Individuals positive outcome (alpha_i = -Inf) omitted, fixest. Negative binomial gamma within fits: dummy-variable intercepts joint maximum likelihood fit. negative binomial fit drops individuals whose outcome always zero. Two-way fits (Gaussian, Poisson, negative binomial): list individual time effects, normalized time effects average zero. conditional logit (family = "binomial", one-way two-way) fixed-effects ordered logit condition individual effects likelihood estimate : fixef() stops error. individual intercepts consistently estimable fixed number periods anyway (incidental parameters). panhurdle() fits: dummy-variable intercepts zero-truncated count part (individuals least one positive count); binary part conditional logit.

Binomial, gamma, beta, Tobit ordered random intercepts, normal link scale: posterior mean computed adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature R nodes fit, centred posterior mode scaled curvature , rule used likelihood. R = 1 (Laplace) mean mode. Poisson negative binomial random intercepts (Hausman, Hall Griliches), whose mixing distribution normal: effect reported log scale multiplicative effect mean. Poisson-gamma model nu_i ~ Gamma(d, d) posterior Gamma(d + sum_t y_it, d + sum_t exp(x_it' beta)), posterior mean log(nu_i) digamma(d + Y_i) - log(d + L_i) mode log((d + Y_i) / (d + L_i)). beta-mixed negative binomial model effect log(delta_i), delta_i / (1 + delta_i) distributed Beta(b, ), giving digamma(b + Y_i) - digamma(+ L_i) log((b + Y_i) / (+ L_i)). Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> lag(lche, 1)  0.79999    0.06043  13.238   <2e-16 *** #> lgdp          0.15476    0.09996   1.548    0.122     #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Arellano-Bond AR(1) test: z = -11.51, p = < 2.2e-16 #> Arellano-Bond AR(2) test: z = 0.418, p = 0.676 #> Sargan test (not robust): chi2(42) = 161.4, p = 6.752e-16 #> Hansen J test (robust): chi2(42) = 65.94, p = 0.0106 #> Wald test for coefficients: chi2(2) = 365, p = < 2.2e-16 #>  b <- coef(gs) b[["lgdp"]] / (1 - b[["lag(lche, 1)"]])   # long-run income elasticity #> [1] 0.7737543  ## Hausman-Taylor: income endogenous; ageing and region exogenous ht <- paniv(lche ~ lgdp + pop65 + region | pop65 + region,             data = hs, index = ix, model = "hausmantaylor") coef(ht) #>                                             (Intercept)  #>                                            -3.380823494  #>                                                    lgdp  #>                                             1.019289147  #>                                                   pop65  #>                                             0.043322428  #>                             regionEurope & Central Asia  #>                                            -0.080872877  #>                         regionLatin America & Caribbean  #>                                             0.047087247  #> regionMiddle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan  #>                                            -0.051324970  #>                                     regionNorth America  #>                                             0.477931406  #>                                        regionSouth Asia  #>                                            -0.245957148  #>                                regionSub-Saharan Africa  #>                                             0.002156185   ## out-of-pocket share, a proportion: beta regression hs$oopshare <- hs$oop / 100 bp <- panglm(oopshare ~ lgdp + pop65, data = hs, index = ix,              model = "pooling", family = "beta", vcov = "cluster") coef(bp) #>   (Intercept)          lgdp         pop65  #>  1.041328e+00 -1.844259e-01 -3.140689e-05   ## quantile heterogeneity of the elasticity coef(panqr(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, tau = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9),            model = "mmqr")) #>       tau=0.1  tau=0.5  tau=0.9 #> lgdp 1.179659 1.149445 1.118256  # \donttest{ ## random-effects beta with Mundlak terms, every fifth year (slower) hs5 <- subset(hs, year %% 5 == 0) br <- panglm(oopshare ~ lgdp + pop65, data = hs5, index = ix,              model = "random", family = "beta", cre = TRUE,              vcov = "cluster", R = 7) summary(br) #>  #> Call: #> panglm(formula = oopshare ~ lgdp + pop65, data = hs5, index = ix,  #>     model = "random", family = "beta", vcov = "cluster", cre = TRUE,  #>     R = 7) #>  #> Family: beta  Link: logit  Model: random  Effect: individual  #> n = 916  groups = 186  vcov: cluster  #>  #> Coefficients: #>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> (Intercept)  1.77971    0.68937   2.582 0.009833 **  #> lgdp        -0.19501    0.10056  -1.939 0.052476 .   #> pop65       -0.04780    0.01323  -3.613 0.000302 *** #> mean_lgdp   -0.08168    0.12642  -0.646 0.518234     #> mean_pop65   0.04828    0.01724   2.801 0.005101 **  #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Log-likelihood: 911.1  #> Dispersion parameter: 0.02356  #> Random-intercept SD: 0.9156  #> Mundlak test (individual means jointly zero): chi2(2) = 8.734, p = 0.01269 #> Residual df: 909  Iterations: 84 #>   ## country-specific income slopes (centre the regressor first) hs$lgdpc <- hs$lgdp - 9 rs <- panglm(lche ~ lgdpc, data = hs, index = ix, model = "random",              random = ~ lgdpc, R = 7) summary(rs) #>  #> Call: #> panglm(formula = lche ~ lgdpc, data = hs, index = ix, model = "random",  #>     random = ~lgdpc, R = 7) #>  #> Family: gaussian  Link: identity  Model: random  Effect: individual  #> n = 4222  groups = 186  vcov: classical  #>  #> Coefficients: #>             Estimate Std. what: panglm: Generalized Linear Models for Panel Data — panglm-package
title: panglm: Generalized Linear Models for Panel Data — panglm-package
text: Provides generalized linear models panel data, including pooled, fixed-effects, random-effects estimators continuous, binary, count, ordinal, positive (gamma), bounded (beta) outcomes, fixed-effects ordered logit Baetschmann, Staub Winkelmann (2015) doi:10.1111/rssa.12090  beta regression (Ferrari Cribari-Neto 2004) doi:10.1080/0266476042000214501 . Also offers correlated random effects (Mundlak 1978) doi:10.2307/1913646 , dynamic models Wooldridge (2005) doi:10.1002/jae.770  initial conditions solution, observation weights, average partial effects, regression-spline curves linearity tests, difference--differences event studies, two-part models costs (Duan et al. 1983) doi:10.1080/07350015.1983.10509330 , including correlated random intercepts (Van Ourti 2004) doi:10.1002/hec.920 . Estimators tests follow standard panel-data references, including Hausman (1978) doi:10.2307/1913827 , Chamberlain (1980) doi:10.2307/2297110 , Allison Waterman (2002) doi:10.1111/1467-9531.00117 , Croissant Millo (2008) doi:10.18637/jss.v027.i02 . Core numerical routines implemented using 'Rcpp', 'RcppArmadillo', 'RcppParallel'.

code: # Habit persistence in smoking: cigarettes per day depend on last # wave's consumption (state dependence) and on the price of tobacco, # with a permanent individual propensity to smoke. The lagged outcome is # correlated with that propensity, so pooled OLS overstates persistence # and the within estimator understates it (Nickell bias); GMM is # consistent. True values: persistence 0.5, price -0.3. set.seed(1) N <- 300; TT <- 7 d <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(N), each = TT), wave = rep(seq_len(TT), N)) propensity <- rnorm(N) d$price <- rnorm(N * TT) d$cigs <- NA for (i in seq_len(N)) {   r <- (i - 1) * TT + seq_len(TT)   y <- propensity[i] / 0.5 + rnorm(1)   for (t in seq_len(TT)) {     y <- 0.5 * y - 0.3 * d$price[r[t]] + propensity[i] + rnorm(1)     d$cigs[r[t]] <- y   } }  # Arellano-Bond difference GMM, two-step with Windmeijer standard errors ab <- pangmm(cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99), data = d,              index = c("id", "wave"), model = "twostep") summary(ab) #>  #> Call: #> pangmm(formula = cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99),  #>     data = d, index = c("id", "wave"), model = "twostep") #>  #> Estimator: two-way two-step difference GMM (Arellano-Bond)  #> n = 1500  groups = 300  T = 7  instruments = 21  #> vcov: robust (Windmeijer)  #>  #> Coefficients: #>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> lag(cigs, 1)  0.55025    0.04883  11.268   <2e-16 *** #> price        -0.27276    0.03055  -8.927   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Arellano-Bond AR(1) test: z = -10.24, p = < 2.2e-16 #> Arellano-Bond AR(2) test: z = -0.9451, p = 0.3446 #> Sargan test (not robust): chi2(14) = 7.391, p = 0.9186 #> Hansen J test (robust): chi2(14) = 6.259, p = 0.9595 #> Wald test for coefficients: chi2(2) = 194.5, p = < 2.2e-16 #>   # Blundell-Bond system GMM with collapsed instruments and at most three # lags of the outcome as instruments bb <- pangmm(cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99), data = d,              index = c("id", "wave"), transformation = "ld",              model = "twostep", collapse = TRUE, maxlag = 4) summary(bb) #>  #> Call: #> pangmm(formula = cigs ~ lag(cigs, 1) + price | lag(cigs, 2:99),  #>     data = d, index = c("id", "wave"), transformation = "ld",  #>     model = "twostep", collapse = TRUE, maxlag = 4) #>  #> Estimator: two-way two-step system GMM (Blundell-Bond)  #> n = 3300  groups = 300  T = 7  instruments = 12  #> vcov: robust (Windmeijer)  #>  #> Coefficients: #>              Estimate Std. code: # Simulated panel of 300 patients over 6 years. Annual health costs have # a patient effect and a heavy upper tail that widens with chronic # conditions: a location-scale model in which the effect of chronic # conditions grows across the cost distribution. set.seed(1) N <- 300; TT <- 6 d <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(N), each = TT), year = rep(seq_len(TT), N)) alpha <- rep(rnorm(N), each = TT) d$chronic <- rpois(N * TT, 1 + 0.5 * (alpha > 0)) d$age <- rep(sample(40:70, N, TRUE), each = TT) + d$year d$cost <- 2 + alpha + 0.5 * d$chronic + 0.02 * d$age +   (1 + 0.3 * d$chronic) * rexp(N * TT)  if (requireNamespace("quantreg", quietly = TRUE)) {   # median and upper tail of costs, MM-QR with analytic standard errors   mm <- panqr(cost ~ chronic + age, data = d, index = c("id", "year"),               tau = c(0.5, 0.9), model = "mmqr")   summary(mm)    # Canay two-step estimator with a small cluster bootstrap   cn <- panqr(cost ~ chronic + age, data = d, index = c("id", "year"),               tau = 0.9, model = "canay", boot = 50, seed = 1)   coef(cn) } #> Warning: 0.1% of the fitted values of the scale function are not positive #> Warning: Solution may be nonunique #> Warning: Solution may be nonunique #> (Intercept)     chronic         age  #>  4.11072454  1.19437845  0.02214631

code: # Simulated cohort of 300 patients followed over 4 waves. A quality of # life score is observed only for patients who answer the questionnaire; # non-response depends on the same health shock that lowers the score, # and on a reminder letter that does not affect the score itself. set.seed(1) N <- 300; TT <- 4 d <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(N), each = TT), wave = rep(seq_len(TT), N)) alpha <- rep(rnorm(N), each = TT) d$treat <- rnorm(N * TT) + 0.5 * alpha d$reminder <- rnorm(N * TT) v <- rnorm(N * TT) u <- 0.7 * v + rnorm(N * TT, sd = 0.7) d$respond <- as.numeric(0.3 + 0.5 * d$treat + d$reminder + 0.3 * alpha + v > 0) d$qol <- ifelse(d$respond == 1, 1 + 0.5 * d$treat + alpha + u, NA)  fit <- panselect(respond ~ treat + reminder, qol ~ treat, data = d,                  index = c("id", "wave"), model = "within", boot = 49, seed = 2) summary(fit) #>  #> Call: #> panselect(selection = respond ~ treat + reminder, outcome = qol ~  #>     treat, data = d, index = c("id", "wave"), model = "within",  #>     boot = 49, seed = 2) #>  #> Wooldridge (1995) panel selection correction: fixed effects with Mundlak means, inverse Mills ratio by period  #> Selection sample: n = 1200  groups = 300  #> Outcome sample:   n = 710  groups = 286  #> Probits fitted for periods: 1, 2, 3, 4  #>  #> Outcome equation (vcov: panel bootstrap, 49 replicates): #>          Estimate Std. title: panglm 1.6.0
text: model = "": (individual means) estimator Gaussian family (plm). tobitfamily(left, right): censored outcomes, pooled random intercept (AER, censReg). orderedfamily(): ordered logit probit, pooled, random intercept, fixed-effects ordered logit “blow-cluster” (Baetschmann, Staub Winkelmann 2015). betafamily(): beta regression outcomes (0, 1), pooled random intercept (betareg, glmmTMB). gammafamily(): gamma regression log link costs, pooled, fixed effects random intercept. Two-way fixed-effects logit: model = "within", family = "binomial", effect = "twoways" (survival::clogit). Random slopes: panglm(model = "random", random = ~ time), correlated random slopes unstructured covariance. Gaussian fits use exact ML number slopes (lme4); Poisson, logit, probit, negative binomial gamma fits use adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature number slopes (glmmTMB, GLMMadaptive). paniv(): panel instrumental variables (fixed effects, G2SLS EC2SLS random effects, pooled 2SLS) Hausman-Taylor estimator, first-stage F statistics Sargan/Hansen tests (plm). pangmm(): Arellano-Bond difference Blundell-Bond system GMM, one- two-step Windmeijer standard errors, AR Hansen tests, collapsed instruments lag limits; warns instruments outnumber individuals (plm::pgmm). panselect(): Wooldridge (1995) correction attrition death cohort studies (glm, plm, sampleSelection). panqr(): panel quantile regression Canay (2011), MM-QR (Machado Santos Silva 2019) pooling, plot() method (quantreg). panfmm() panfmmselect(): latent class GLMs class membership constant within individual, Poisson, NB2, Gaussian, logit probit components, weights, offsets concomitant model (flexmix). twopart(): two-part models semicontinuous costs, correlated random intercepts (correlated = TRUE). () eventstudy(): two-way fixed-effects difference--differences event studies Gaussian, Poisson, negative binomial binomial (conditional logit) outcomes (fixest, survival::clogit). attgt(): Callaway Sant’Anna (2021) group-time ATTs aggregations, pre-trend test, weights, extra clustering multiplier bootstrap uniform bands (). etwfe(): Wooldridge (2023) extended two-way FE estimator linear, Poisson logit outcomes, weights, xvar ivar (etwfe).

title: panglm 1.1.0
text: CRAN submission candidate. Adds bundled synthetic dataset, copd (simulated COPD follow-panel), runnable @examples every exported function documented method. Added plot.panglm() coefficient, residual, fitted-value views, plot.panglm_hurdle() two hurdle components. Added zero-truncated NB2 positive-count models panglm_hurdle() count_family = "negbin". Added HC1 cluster-robust covariance estimates one-way conditional binomial fixed-effects models. Reorganized package vignette methodological account model specification, estimation, inference, diagnostics, scope. Completed fitted-value prediction semantics across estimators. Random-effects response predictions integrate fitted mixing distribution, fixed-effects predictions include known panel effects, exact conditional binomial fits expose conditional inclusion probabilities. Fitted values residuals now preserve input row order unsorted panels. Corrected likelihood parameter accounting. logLik() now counts fitted dispersion, shape, variance, absorbed fixed-effect parameters belong reported likelihood. Gaussian pooled likelihoods use maximum-likelihood variance retaining unbiased residual variance covariance estimation. glance() now reports AIC, BIC, likelihood degrees freedom. Corrected sandwich inference exact conditional binomial models. HC1 now operates independent stratum scores, custom clusters required preserve complete conditioned strata. Custom cluster vectors now correctly reordered panel supplied index order. Revised fixed-effects NB2 description state dummy-variable estimator remains subject finite-T incidental-parameter concerns short panels. Hardened model-frame handling. Factor interactions retained, unidentified columns reported removed numerical fitting, na.exclude restores fitted values residuals input length, panel indexes checked missing duplicate individual-time keys. Nontrivial weights nonzero offsets now fail explicitly instead risking apparently successful fit ignores .

title: panglm 0.1.0
text: model = "pooling": gaussian/poisson/binomial GLM via IRLS, genuine NB2 (negative binomial) via theta-profiled IRLS – matches MASS::glm.nb() exactly. (family = "negbin" previously silently aliased Poisson every model level; fixed everywhere .) model = "within": gaussian (exact demeaning, one-way effect = "twoways"), poisson (conditional MLE, one-way effect = "twoways" via outer-IRLS/inner-weighted-FWL – algorithm behind fixest::feglm()), negative binomial (Allison & Waterman 2002 unconditional dummy-variable estimator – matches fixest::fenegbin() exactly; tractable small--moderate N, intended large panels), binomial (exact conditional logistic regression, Chamberlain 1980 – matches survival::clogit(method = "exact"), pglm equivalent). effect = "twoways" available gaussian, poisson, negbin (latter two via outer-IRLS/inner-weighted-FWL, matching fixest::fenegbin() exactly); yet binomial (general closed-form two-way conditional logit exists). Groups -zero outcome now dropped (informative message()) fitting Allison-Waterman FE-NB2 estimator – dummy-variable intercept unbounded log link, boundary case model = "within", family = "binomial" already screened . Previously left , contaminate shared covariate coefficients via joint solve, just offending group’s intercept. model = "random": gaussian (Swamy-Arora), poisson (Poisson-Gamma, single dispersion parameter), negative binomial (genuinely different, 2-parameter beta-negative-binomial mixture matching pglm’s lnl.negbin.R exactly – previously aliased Poisson-Gamma model), binomial (Gauss-Hermite quadrature) random effects. random-effects Poisson fit now seeds pooled-Poisson MLE plus method--moments dispersion estimate, uses Levenberg-Marquardt/ridge damping (warning engages) instead erroring singular Hessian – verified heavily zero-inflated, extremely skewed panels previously crashed.

title: panglm 0.1.0
text: vcov(fit, type = "HC1" | "cluster") pooled/within models, including effect = "twoways" (gaussian) within negbin (Allison-Waterman): sandwich correction uses full covariate+dummy score bread ((k+G) parameters), just covariate block, since dummy intercepts jointly estimated contribute sampling variability . Random-effects models intentionally keep model-based (information-matrix) SEs , matching lme4/glmmTMB convention. confint.panglm() – Wald intervals using whichever vcov fit currently carries. panglm_dispersiontest() – Pearson chi-squared/df overdispersion test poisson/negbin fits available fitted.values. Observations zero unavailable fitted value (e.g. rows -zero group screened fixed-effects negbin fit) excluded statistic rather producing 0/0 = NaN; excluded count reported n_excluded returned object. panglm_hausman() FE-vs-RE specification testing. tidy()/glance() methods registered generics::tidy/glance broom/modelsummary compatibility.

title: panglm 0.1.0
text: panglm_hurdle(): fixed-effects hurdle model panels structural zeros (pattern shows extreme, family-invariant overdispersion either family = "poisson" family = "negbin" panglm()). Fits 1(y>0) via existing conditional-logit FE estimator, zero-truncated Poisson NB2 FE model (Allison-Waterman-style dummy-variable estimator, Newton-Raphson exact Fisher information) y>0 subsample. truncated-Poisson math (fixed effects) matches pscl::hurdle()’s count part exactly. zero-truncated likelihoods validated pscl::hurdle().
